disclaimer: These are PermissionGuard application-specific detection rules INFORMED BY OWASP guidance. They are NOT official OWASP automated tests, NOT MASTG test executions, and NOT MASVS certifications. Where a formal requirement applies it is referenced by ID; otherwise the check is labelled as an application-specific rule informed by OWASP.

masvs_mapping.MASVS-PRIVACY-1: The app does not unnecessarily access sensitive data or device identifiers.
masvs_mapping.MASVS-PRIVACY-2: The app only accesses the minimum data required for its stated purpose (data minimisation).
masvs_mapping.MASVS-PRIVACY-3: Data is handled according to privacy best practices (collection, disclosure, retention).

rules.title: Excessive permission requests beyond declared functionality
rules.description: The application requests permissions that are not required by any feature implied by its declared category. This is an application-specific check informed by OWASP's data minimisation principle (MASWE-0066: excessive permissions).
rules.assessment_logic: For each dangerous permission outside the category's expected set, raise POTENTIAL_CONCERN with evidence naming both the permission and the category.
rules.remediation: Remove the unneeded permission, or gate it behind an explicit user-triggered feature with a clear rationale.
rules.limitations: Purpose is user-declared; some legitimate uses may not be covered by our category profiles.

rules.title: Sensitive data access without a less-intrusive alternative
rules.description: Where a known less-intrusive alternative exists for a requested permission (e.g. Photo Picker instead of full media access, ACTION_DIAL instead of CALL_PHONE), its use should be preferred.
rules.assessment_logic: If the knowledge base lists alternatives for a requested permission AND the permission is not expected for the category: raise LOW-severity finding recommending the alternative.
rules.remediation: Adopt the documented alternative: apply the 'alternatives' entry from the permission's knowledge-base record.
rules.limitations: Architectural constraints may make the alternative impractical without deeper code review.

rules.title: Missing justification for sensitive access
rules.description: High/critical-sensitivity permissions should map to a documented user benefit. Access without a traceable rationale prevents informed consent.
rules.assessment_logic: If a HIGH/CRITICAL permission is UNEXPECTED for the category: POTENTIAL_CONCERN (HIGH). If purpose unknown: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE with a prompt to supply the purpose.
rules.remediation: Document the user-facing feature that requires the data, or remove the permission.
rules.limitations: Does not inspect the app's privacy policy or store listing.

rules.title: Permission combination increases privacy exposure
rules.description: Certain permission combinations multiply privacy impact (e.g. identifier + precise location + network). Individual permission review misses this compounding risk.
rules.assessment_logic: Delegated to the combination detector; each hit raises an indicator finding with severity from the combination rule.
rules.remediation: Split data flows, reduce scope, or drop the least-justified permission of the pair.
rules.limitations: Combinations are indicators for review, not proof of data flow between the permissions.

rules.title: Platform anti-abuse features weakened
rules.description: Flags manifest configurations that weaken platform protections: debuggable builds, cleartext traffic, unrestricted backup, or shared UID — each increases exposure if the app handles sensitive data.
rules.assessment_logic: debuggable=true -> HIGH finding; cleartext=true -> MEDIUM; allowBackup=true -> LOW (INFO for enterprise); sharedUserId -> HIGH.
rules.remediation: Disable debugging in release builds, enable network security config, restrict backup rules.
rules.limitations: Manifest attributes only; runtime instrumentation protections are not evaluated.
